election: Selection as chairman of the PLO Executive Committee
role_sought: Chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization
detail: Named head of the PLO by its Executive Committee after Yasser Arafat's death on 11 November 2004 (Britannica). On 25 November 2004 Fatah's Revolutionary Council endorsed him as its candidate for the presidential election of 9 January 2005 (Wikipedia).

role_sought: President of the Palestinian National Authority
vote_share: 501,448 votes: 62.52% of the 802,077 ballots cast, 67.38% of valid votes
opponent: Mustafa Barghouti (Palestinian National Initiative, independent; 156,227 votes, 19.48% of ballots cast) and five other candidates
detail: First presidential election since 1996, held to succeed Yasser Arafat and organised by the Central Elections Commission (CEC); Hamas and Islamic Jihad boycotted it. Turnout was 73.4% of registered voters according to Wikipedia's summary; the CEC extended voting by two hours and let unregistered voters vote with their identity cards, which raised fears of multiple voting. Wikipedia reports that Israeli forces arrested or restricted the movement of other candidates during the campaign, including Mustafa Barghouti. The CEC's results table (a PDF the harvest is not allowed to read under the CEC's robots.txt) gives 62.52% for Abbas as a share of all voters; Wikipedia's summary gives 67.38% of valid votes from the same counts. Elected for four years, he was sworn in on 15 January 2005; no presidential election has been held since.

election: Vote of the PLO Central Council on the presidency of the State of Palestine
role_sought: President of the State of Palestine
detail: The PLO Central Council chose him as President of the State of Palestine on 23 November 2008 according to Wikipedia (citing AFP); his official biography gives 14 October 2008.

The first Fatah general conference since 1989 elected him chairman of the movement (Wikipedia); Anadolu Agency and other reports describe the 2016 vote as a re-election in similar circumstances, without a contested ballot.

election: Vote of the PLO Central Council on the extension of the presidential term
role_sought: Continuation as President of the Palestinian National Authority
result: Term extended until elections can be held
detail: With the January 2010 elections not held because of the Fatah–Hamas split, the PLO Central Council extended his term (and that of the Legislative Council) indefinitely until new elections. Hamas had argued that his term ended on 9 January 2009 and that the Speaker of the Legislative Council, Aziz Duwaik, should act as president; it withdrew its objection when the April 2014 unity agreement was signed.

vote_share: Unanimous (by acclamation, at the opening session)
detail: Congress spokesman Mahmoud Abu al-Haija announced that he had been 'elected unanimously at the first session of the congress', according to Anadolu Agency citing WAFA.

The conference of 2,514 members, the first in ten years, re-elected him chairman unanimously on its opening day, before electing the Central Committee and Revolutionary Council; Nasser al-Qudwa, the only Central Committee member to boycott it, told Al Jazeera that Abbas had 'engineered this meeting to produce the outcome he wants'. In his opening address he pledged to reform the Palestinian Authority and hold the long-delayed elections.
